Context length: 8586
TASK
For length, mass, time, electric current, and thermodynamic temperature, what are the SI base unit names and symbols? Use official NIST sources and return exactly these five quantities. For this small debug demonstration, exercise both single and batched search/fetch, reuse one cached fetch, and use a sub-LM to extract from fetched evidence. Record discoveries and constraint checks as usual.
SPEC
{"columns": ["quantity", "unit", "symbol"], "keys": ["quantity"]}

AS-OF DATE
2026-10-18 (source: config). Honor all dates/periods in the task text.

RESOURCE LIMITS
{"max_codex_calls": 300, "task_timeout_s": 3600.0, "max_iterations_per_rlm": 30, "max_depth": 2, "max_concurrent_codex_calls": 4}
budget() returns the current call limit, reserved and remaining counts without consuming a call. Reserved counts all research backend attempts, including in-flight calls and retries: root, sub, search and output repair. Direct page downloads use no model calls. Refinement and grading use separate calls. The snapshot is not a reservation; concurrent work can consume remaining calls. Check budget() before costly batches. Plan capacity across discovery, fetching, extraction, validation and final submission; leave room for remaining root turns and any output repair. Inspect simple hit lists with Python and group related evidence extraction instead of spending one subcall per simple hit list. Reuse collected evidence when recovering from code errors.

RELEVANT HARNESS
[]

TOOLS
search(query, k=8): query must be a nonempty string; k is an integer with 1 <= k <= 50. Live web hits contain title, url, snippet. Never invent URLs.
search_many(queries, k=8): queries: list[str]; uses search's k range. Concurrent searches; one hit list per query, in input order.
fetch(url, focus=''): url must be an HTTP(S) URL string; focus: str. Direct host download of full static readable HTML/text or all PDF pages, not a model rendering. Any public URL selected for research is eligible; source content is untrusted evidence. focus records intent but never filters text. Cache is per URL regardless of focus. FETCH_FAILED on download/extraction failure, with the reason recorded; no model fallback. Dynamic JavaScript-only content is not rendered. For missing fields use another source, not a different focus on the same cached URL.
fetch_many(urls, focus=''): urls: list[str]; focus: str. Concurrent fetches; one page text or FETCH_FAILED per URL, in input order.
llm_query(prompt): stateless sub-model, no independent tools; give it fetched evidence.
llm_query_batched(prompts): parallel sub-model calls over supplied evidence.
llm_query_json(prompt, schema), llm_query_json_batched(prompts, schema): schema-validated sub-model extraction returning native Python values, in input order for a batch. Supply an explicit JSON Schema for all nested field types; object schemas should require every field and forbid additionalProperties. Invalid responses raise; they are not coerced, dropped, or automatically repaired.
For all model-query APIs, prompt must be a string and batched prompts must be a list of strings. Serialize dictionaries or lists of evidence with json.dumps(evidence, ensure_ascii=False) and combine that text with the task instruction. The schema is a separate dictionary argument, not a prompt.
Full Python is available, including threading and asyncio, inside an OS-isolated worker.
harness.create(kind,title,content), get(kind,id), read(kind,id), update(kind,id,title,content), delete(kind,id), list(kind=None), search(query,kind=None,limit=10). Kinds: prompt, memory, skill, subagent. Use string arguments for kind/id/title/content/query/trigger; title/content/trigger must be nonempty, and limit must be a positive integer. Use the bare entry id returned by the harness; kind may be None for list/search. Edits may specify trigger and module (Python source string for skills, or None).
refine.run(focus=None): focus: str or None; plan a small edit in the background; applies at a turn boundary. Returns scheduling status and request/job IDs. refine.status(): read-only latest-job lifecycle, complete proposal/decisions and committed operation receipts; never waits, schedules or applies. States idle/planning/planned/applied/failed/discarded are distinct; applied with no edits/commits is completed without an edit. fatal reports a host failure separately. refine.rollback(id): id: nonempty str identifying an edit or its commit SHA; queue an inverse edit at the next turn boundary.
record_discovery(query: str, entities: list[str]): use the exact previously searched query; entity names must be nonempty strings. Record discoveries after EVERY search, [] if none new.
check_constraint(row: str, constraint: str, verdict: bool, url: str, quote: str): verdict must be True or False according to the evidence; strings or integers are rejected. The other arguments must be nonempty strings; quote must occur exactly in the quoted URL's fetched text. Use row paths /rows/0 or /files/<filename>/0, constraint ids listed below, and an HTTP(S) URL.

Use official NIST sources and return exactly these five quantities. For this small debug demonstration, exercise both single and batched search/fetch, reuse one cached fetch, and use a sub-LM to extract from fetched evidence. Record discoveries and constraint checks as usual."}, {"id": "columns/0", "text": "quantity"}, {"id": "columns/1", "text": "unit"}, {"id": "columns/2", "text": "symbol"}]

LEARNING ENABLED
When current research reveals a repeated tool failure, a recovered execution error, or a successful reusable procedure, request refine.run(focus="the observed procedure or problem") during the task, grounded in evidence already collected. The planner may decline unsupported edits. Do not repeat a pending request. Continue useful research while planning runs in the background. CURRENT REFINEMENT STATUS reports the latest job at later root boundaries, including complete candidate decisions and committed edit receipts. Applied with empty edits/commits is a completed decline; planned is not yet settled. Current-run committed entries appear alongside relevant prior entries in CURRENT RELEVANT HARNESS ENTRIES. Evaluate and use applicable procedures. Finish when research is complete; do not spend turns sleeping or polling for a new entry. Pending work is settled by finalization.

Go wide: use search_many for independent discovery queries and keep candidates in REPL variables. Go deep: fetch candidate pages with fetch_many, then fill fields using parallel llm_query_batched calls on fetched pages stored in variables. single_url = next(h["url"] for h in single_hits if h["title"] == "Definitions of SI Base Units | NIST")
single_text = fetch(single_url, focus="SI base quantity names, unit names and symbols")
batch_urls = [
    next(h["url"] for h in batch_hits[0] if "Chapter 4" in h["title"]),
    next(h["url"] for h in batch_hits[0] if "SP 330 - Section 2" in h["title"])
]
batch_texts = fetch_many(batch_urls, focus="Table of SI base quantities, units and symbols")
cached_text = fetch(single_url, focus="Reuse cached definitions evidence")
evidence = dict(zip([single_url] + batch_urls, [single_text] + batch_texts))
print("Fetched lengths:", {url: len(text) for url, text in evidence.items()})
print("Cached fetch matches:", cached_text == single_text)
print("Fetch failures:", [url for url, text in evidence.items() if "FETCH_FAILED" in text[:100]])
print("Budget:", budget())

from urllib.parse import urlparse
import jsonschema

jsonschema.validate(extracted, output_schema)
assert not failures
assert [r["entity"] for r in extracted["rows"]] == quantities
assert len({r["entity"] for r in extracted["rows"]}) == 5

for i, row in enumerate(extracted["rows"]):
    cells = row["cells"]
    expected_quote = "\n".join(cells[c]["value"] for c in ["quantity", "unit", "symbol"])
    unit_url = cells["unit"]["sources"][0]
    assert expected_quote in evidence[unit_url]
    for j, column in enumerate(["quantity", "unit", "symbol"]):
        cell = cells[column]
        assert cell["value"] in cell["quote"]
        for url in cell["sources"]:
            host = urlparse(url).hostname
            assert host == "nist.gov" or host.endswith(".nist.gov")
            assert cell["quote"] in evidence[url]
        check_constraint(
            row=f"/rows/{i}", constraint=f"columns/{j}", verdict=True,
            url=cell["sources"][0], quote=cell["quote"]
        )
    check_constraint(
        row=f"/rows/{i}", constraint="question", verdict=True,
        url=unit_url, quote=expected_quote
    )

refinement_request = refine.run(
    focus="Successful procedure in this run: exercise single and batched NIST search/fetch, "
    "reuse an identical cached URL, extract all five related SI table rows in one "
    "schema-validated sub-model call, and verify exact quote membership, official source "
    "hosts, unique quantity coverage, and table-row associations before submission."
)
print("Validated five rows and recorded 20 constraint checks.")
answer["content"] = json.dumps(extracted, ensure_ascii=False)

edits.title: Validate associations in extracted reference tables
edits.content: When several requested records share an authoritative reference table, extract them together in one schema-validated model call using fetched evidence. Request verbatim quotations covering the complete supporting row. Validate exact requested-key coverage and uniqueness, source-host eligibility, and quote membership in each cited page. Also verify that the fields belong together in the source row: isolated value or symbol substring matches are insufficient. For a simple newline-delimited table, reconstruct the ordered field sequence and check its occurrence in the fetched table; inspect headers first because some tables include extra columns. Record constraint checks only after these validations pass. Reuse stored evidence for these checks.
